title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། ཇེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 176)
shelf_note: A Pramana commentary (Dharmottara-style gloss on the Nyayabindu's viruddha-karana / viruddha-karya examples: fire vs. horripilation, smoke in a place) in the Derge Tengyur tshad ma section; belongs on the shelf.

ocr_errors.problem: editorial variant brace markup {a,b} carried into the reader transcription; the block print has only སོགས

tr_errors_A.english: When causes are mutually incompatible, apprehending the cause merely conveys that contradiction.
tr_errors_A.problem: the point is that only the apprehension of the (incompatible) cause is what makes the absence known; 'merely conveys that contradiction' blurs the claim

tr_errors_A.english: If the person were the subject, the property of the subject would fail to be the valid logical reason
tr_errors_A.problem: garbled: should be 'the reason would not be a property of the subject (pakṣadharma)'; A inverts subject and predicate of the clause, though the following 'because smoke is the property of the locus' keeps the argument recoverable

tr_errors_A.english: a person in whose vicinity a specific attribute of fire is present
tr_errors_A.problem: མེའི་ཁྱད་པར = a particular (kind of) fire, not an 'attribute of fire'

tr_errors_B.english: For example, in a person who exhibits symptoms such as goosebumps
tr_errors_B.problem: the example statement is negative ('in this person there are NO particular states such as horripilation'); B drops མེད and makes the person exhibit the symptoms, reversing the very thesis the whole passage proves

tr_errors_B.english: There is no contradiction in the definition.
tr_errors_B.problem: page opens mid-word of རྒྱུ་མཚན (cause/reason), as the next sentence's གྲང་བའི་རྒྱུ་མཚན shows; 'definition' is a guess

tr_errors_B.english: a person in a particular location who possesses the distinct symptoms of goosebumps caused by cold is described in that way
tr_errors_B.problem: the gloss names the PLACE that has such a person, not the person; B shifts the referent, which is exactly the point the next sentence (mentioning the place) depends on

pages.prefer_reason: B drops the negation in the core example ('no horripilation in this person' becomes 'a person who exhibits goosebumps'), reversing the thesis, while A's slips are moderate and recoverable.

book_verdict: A clean, correctly matched Derge pramāṇa folio with a near-perfect transcription; translation A is a serviceable reading, while translation B reverses the key negative example and should not be shown.
